treaty_name: Convention between Ireland and Belgium for the avoidance of double taxation and the prevention of fiscal evasion with respect to taxes on income (1970, as amended 2014)
source_title: Revenue.ie: Ireland-Belgium Convention 1970, Protocol 2014, MLI synthesised text

rates.quote: Such dividends may also be taxed in the Contracting State of which the company paying the dividends is a resident and according to the law of that State. However a. the tax so charged shall not exceed 15 per cent of the gross amount of the said dividends paid by a company which is a resident of Belgium;

Such interest may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises, and according to the law of that State. However, the tax so charged shall not exceed 15 per cent of the amount of the interest.
Royalties arising in a Contracting State and paid to a resident of the other Contracting State shall be taxable only in that other State.

ppt.quote: Notwithstanding any provisions of this Convention, a benefit under this Convention shall not be granted in respect of an item of income if it is reasonable to conclude, having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction that resulted directly or indirectly in that benefit, unless it is established that granting that benefit in these circumstances would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of this Convention.

notes: Dividends: Art. 10(2) caps only Belgian-source dividends (15%); for Irish-source dividends Art. 10(2)(b) only exempts them from Irish sur-tax and sets no rate limit, so no Ireland-source dividend cap is modelled (source_state BE). Interest article excludes from "interest" (and sends to Arts. 7/22) commercial hire-purchase credit interest, bank-to-bank current account interest and bank deposit interest not represented by bearer bonds. 2014 Protocol amends only competent authority definition and exchange of information. valid_from: Belgian WHT on income credited/payable after 31 Dec of ratification year (1973). MLI WHT effect 1 Jan 2020 per synthesised text; no MLI Art. 8 box.
